summary: Huawen Bai was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied at Peking University from circa 1951 to 1955 and later served there as a professor around 1955.

Hubert Decleer worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Koninklijk Atheneum Oostende, Hotel- en Toerismeschool Spermalie, and KU Leuven under Étienne Lamotte. He held posts at Alliance Française (1980–1987) and SIT Graduate Institute (1987–1999).

Hubert Durt was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Étienne Lamotte (circa 1961–1969). He served as a professor at École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1970–1998) and International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~1996–2011), and directed the Hōbōgirin Institute (~1980).

Hugh B. Urban is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (~1992–1998) under Wendy Doniger, and became an associate professor at Ohio State University around 1998.
Hugh Gray was an Indologist. He studied at Battersea Grammar School and held a post at the University of Cambridge.
Hugh J. Silverman was a philosopher who studied at Stanford University until circa 1973. He held academic posts at the University of Vienna, the University of Klagenfurt, and the University of Turin.

Hugh Richardson was a scholar in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He studied at Keble College (~1924–1928) and under Basil Gould (1934), and served in the Indian Civil Service from circa 1930 to 1950.

Hugo David is an Indologist and philosopher. He completed his PhD at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~2005–2012). He held a fellowship at the University of Cambridge (2013–2014) and became a permanent member at École française d'Extrême-Orient in 2015.
Hui-tzu Lu is a scholar of Sinology and history and archaeology. She studied under doctoral supervisor Chia-lin Pao Tao, as well as Jing-shen Tao, Zhiru Shi, and Zhihui Shi.
Huidi Zeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Fo Guang University (~2008–2011) under the supervision of Yi-hsun Huang.

Huimin is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1986–1992). He served as executive director at Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (~1992), professor at Taipei National University of the Arts (~1999), and president of Dharma Drum Buddhist College (~2007–2014).
Huishan Lin is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University from circa 2006 to 2009 under the supervision of Kuo-wei Liu.

Huiwen Zhuang is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University (~2006–2009) under supervisor Kirill Jurievitch Solonin, and also studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun.
Huiyu Zhang is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and held a lecturing post at Dongguk University in 1996.

Humberto Maturana was a philosopher and scientist who studied at Liceo Manuel de Salas, University College London (~1954–1956), and Harvard University (~1956–1958). He held a post at the University of Chile around 1960.
Hung-Yi Yang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a PhD at the University of Sydney between circa 2008 and 2013 under the supervision of Mark Allon.

Huston Smith worked in religious studies and philosophy after studying at Central Methodist University and the University of Chicago. He was a philosophy professor at MIT (~1958–1973), professor at Syracuse University (~1973–1989), and visiting professor at UC Berkeley (~1989–2004).
Huynh Thi Ha Vy is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kapila Abhayawansa and earned a Master of Arts degree at the International Buddhist College between circa 2013 and 2015.

Hyejeong Choi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. She completed a PhD at Ohio State University (~2009–2015) under John C. Huntington and served as a visiting researcher at the Archaeological Institute of Kashihara, Nara Prefecture.

Hyon Gak Sunim is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Yale University (~1983–1987), the University of Freiburg (~1985–1986), Harvard University (~1989–1992), and under traditional teacher Seungsahn (~1989–2004).
